questions.stem: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A) Zuckerberg wrote a letter to his new-born baby girl.
B) Zuckerberg wants his baby girl to grow up in a better world.
C) Zuckerberg became one of the most searched names on Google.
D) Zuckerberg decided to donate most of his Facebook shares.

explain.定位:
Zuckerberg wrote that he and his wife, Priscilla Chan, would donate 99% of his Facebook
stock shares, worth about $45 billion, to do just that.
扎克伯格写道，他和妻子普莉希拉·陈将捐出他所持 Facebook 股票的 99%（价值约 450 亿
美元），以实现这一目标。
explain.信号:
首段落点即核心事件。新闻把最重要的事放在开头：第 1 段先交代写信，紧接着 would
donate 99% of his Facebook stock shares 给出本则新闻分量最重、后文都围绕它展开
（搜索、点赞、税务、捐给哪个机构）的核心动作——"捐出大部分股票"，这就是主旨
落点。
explain.替换:
donate 99% of his Facebook stock shares ↔ donate most of his Facebook shares
99% 概括成 most
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音开头确实说了 wrote a letter to his baby girl，Zuckerberg wrote a letter to his
new-born baby girl. 原词照搬，听到很想选；但写信只是引出"捐股票"的由头，不是新闻
主要内容，属于以细节冒充主旨。
借用原文：wrote a letter to his baby girl
B) 原词陷阱
Zuckerberg wants his baby girl to grow up in a better world. 几乎照搬录音 to grow
up in a world better than ours today，但这只是他捐款背后的"愿望/动机"，新闻报的
是"捐"这个行动本身，愿望撑不起主旨。
借用原文：to grow up in a world better than ours today
C) 原词陷阱
Zuckerberg became one of the most searched names on Google. 对应录音第 2 段
Zuckerberg was one of the most searched names on Google，原词几乎一字不差；但
这是消息发布"之后"的连带反应，是细节，不是新闻主线。
借用原文：Zuckerberg was one of the most searched names on Google

questions.stem: How much are the stock shares to be donated by Zuckerberg worth now?

explain.定位:
Zuckerberg wrote that he and his wife, Priscilla Chan, would donate 99% of his Facebook
stock shares, worth about $45 billion, to do just that.
扎克伯格写道，他和妻子普莉希拉·陈将捐出他所持 Facebook 股票的 99%（价值约 450 亿
美元），以实现这一目标。
explain.信号:
worth 紧跟金额。金额信息由 worth about $45 billion 直接给出，"worth"（价值）一
词后面紧跟的就是题目要的钱数；听到"worth/价值"这类词就该绷紧神经抓后面的数字和
单位。
explain.替换:
worth about $45 billion ↔ About $45 billion.
金额原样照应
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
About $45 million. 数字 45 与录音 $45 billion 相同，专坑把 billion（十亿）听成 million
（百万）的人；数字对了、单位错了就满盘皆输，这是金额题最常见的死法。
借用原文：about $45 billion
B) 未提及
About $50 million. 的 50 在录音里根本没念到，金额是 45 不是 50，属于凭空编造的数
字，用来给没听清的人当退路。
D) 张冠李戴
About $99 billion. 里的 99 来自录音 donate 99% of his Facebook stock shares
的"99%"，把"捐股比例 99%"偷换成"金额 99 billion"，听到"99"就想选的人正中圈套；金
额是 45 billion，不是 99。
借用原文：donate 99% of his Facebook stock shares
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Delegates from almost 200 nations at the UN climate change summit in Paris have reached a draft
agreement on how to move forward on the issue.
来自近200个国家的代表在巴黎联合国气候变化峰会上就如何推进这一议题达成了一份协议草案。
2 The text, which runs to 42 pages, was approved on Saturday after four years' work that started in
Durban in 2011. It presents options for dealing with everything from the long-term goals of combating
climate change, to financial assistance for developing nations that will need help to move away from
fossil fuels. There's a broad political will to come to a global agreement here in Paris and that is good
news. What is still missing in the text is a clear vision to go 100 percent renewable energy by mid-
century, which gives us a chance to help those people who suffer from catastrophic climate change.
这份长达42页的文本于周六获得批准，此前经过了四年的努力，始于2011年在德班启动的进程。它提出
了应对气候变化长期目标到为需要帮助摆脱化石燃料的发展中国家提供财政援助等各方面问题的选项。在
巴黎达成全球协议的广泛政治意愿是存在的,这是个好消息。文本中仍然缺少的是到本世纪中叶实现100%
可再生能源的明确愿景,这将使我们有机会帮助那些遭受灾难性气候变化影响的人们。
3 To draw attention to what they see as the time pressure on the issue, campaigners led by Danish artist
Olafur Eliasson, have installed 12 mini-icebergs in the shape of a clock in the Place le Pantheon. The
ice was brought all the way from Greenland in temperature-controlled containers.
为了引起人们对他们所认为的这一议题时间紧迫性的关注,由丹麦艺术家Olafur Eliasson领导的活动人士
在先贤祠广场安装了12座呈时钟形状排列的迷你冰山。这些冰块是用温控集装箱从格陵兰岛一路运来的。

questions.stem: What can we learn about the draft agreement?
options: A) It was approved on Sunday.
C) It targets rich countries tackling climate change.
D) It has a clear vision to go renewable energy.

explain.定位:
The text, which runs to 42 pages, was approved on Saturday after four years' work that started
in Durban in 2011.
这份文本共42页，在历经从2011年德班启动的四年工作之后，于周六获得通过。
explain.信号:
同位插入语直给页数。答案藏在主语后的插入语 which runs to 42 pages 里——新闻爱用
which/who 引导的插入说明顺带塞进一个关键数据。听到 The text 之后紧跟一个 which
从句报出 42 pages，就该立刻锁定"页数"这一钩子；同句的 approved on Saturday 与
Durban 是来核对其余选项真伪的对照点。
explain.替换:
which runs to 42 pages ↔ It runs to 42 pages.
插入语改写成完整句
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音明说 was approved on Saturday（周六通过），选项 It was approved on Sunday.
盗用了 approved 这个原词，只把 Saturday 偷偷换成 Sunday。听到 approved 就选会中
招——这是新闻在"哪一天"上设的经典原词陷阱。
借用原文：was approved on Saturday
C) 偷换概念
录音说这份文本为 financial assistance for developing nations（向发展中国家提供资
助）作出安排，选项 It targets rich countries tackling climate change. 却说它"针对富
国"。录音借用了 climate change 等原词，但对象由"发展中国家"被换成"rich
countries"，方向完全拧了。
借用原文：financial assistance for developing nations
D) 与原文相反
录音原文是 What is still missing in the text is a clear vision to go 100 percent
renewable energy——"文本里仍然缺少"一份转向可再生能源的清晰愿景。选项 It has a
clear vision to go renewable energy. 盗用了 clear vision、renewable energy 等整串原
词，却把 still missing（仍缺少）反说成 has（已有），与原文极性相反。
借用原文：What is still missing in the text is a clear vision to go 100 percent renewable energy

questions.stem: Where have the twelve mini-icebergs been placed?
options: D) In the Place de la Pantheon.

explain.定位:
campaigners led by Danish artist Olafur Eliasson, have installed 12 mini-icebergs in the shape
of a clock in the Place le Pantheon.
由丹麦艺术家奥拉维尔·埃利亚松带领的活动人士，把12座做成时钟形状的迷你冰山安置在
了先贤祠广场。
explain.信号:
放置动词后即地点。答案信号是"安放"动词 have installed 12 mini-icebergs 后面紧跟的地
点 in the Place le Pantheon。题干问 placed（放在哪），录音用同义的 installed 报出动
作，动作之后第一个 in + 地点就是落点。听到 installed 12 mini-icebergs 立刻把耳朵压
在它后面的地名上。
explain.替换:
in the Place le Pantheon ↔ In the Place de la Pantheon.
同一地名直接对应
have installed 12 mini-icebergs ↔ In the Place de la Pantheon.
installed 等价于题干 placed
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音里 Denmark 的踪迹来自 Danish artist Olafur Eliasson——丹麦只是带队艺术家的国
籍，不是冰山被放的地方。选项 In Denmark. 盗用 Danish 这个原词来骗"听到丹麦就选"，
实则答非所问。
借用原文：Danish artist Olafur Eliasson
B) 答非所问
录音说 The ice was brought all the way from Greenland——格陵兰是冰"运来"的来源，
不是冰山被安置的地点。选项 In Greenland. 正是预读时标记的高危干扰：把"来自哪里"偷
换成"放在哪里"。
借用原文：The ice was brought all the way from Greenland
C) 张冠李戴
Durban 出自上一段 after four years' work that started in Durban in 2011——德班是这
场协议工作"四年前启动"的会议地，与冰山放置毫不相干。选项 In Durban. 借这个背景地
名制造跨段干扰。
借用原文：after four years' work that started in Durban in 2011

questions.stem: Who is Mauricio Macri?
options: B) The chosen successor of Argentina's president.
C) The governor of Buenos Aires province.
D) The mayor of Buenos Aires.

explain.定位:
Mauricio Macri, the mayor of Buenos Aires, finished in second place with 35.2 percent of
the vote.
布宜诺斯艾利斯市市长毛里西奥·马克里以 35.2% 的得票率位居第二。
explain.信号:
人名后的同位语即身份。答案信号是人名紧跟的同位语：Mauricio Macri, the mayor of
Buenos Aires，人名后用逗号补一个头衔，这个 the mayor of Buenos Aires 就是他的身
份，无需推断、直接锁定。
explain.替换:
the mayor of Buenos Aires ↔ The mayor of Buenos Aires.
头衔几乎原样对应
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
The ruling party candidate. 盗用了录音 the ruling party candidate Daniel Scioli，但那
是 Scioli 的身份，不是 Macri 的，把别人的头衔安到 Macri 头上，是对话/多人新闻里最常
见的张冠李戴。
借用原文：the ruling party candidate Daniel Scioli
B) 张冠李戴
The chosen successor of Argentina's president. 来自录音 the chosen successor of
Argentina's president，但原文这话说的是 Scioli，不是 Macri，同样是把 Scioli 的身份移
花接木给 Macri。
借用原文：the chosen successor of Argentina's president
C) 张冠李戴
The governor of Buenos Aires province. 取自录音 Mr. Scioli is governor of Buenos
Aires province，那是 Scioli 的职务；和 D 的 mayor 只差一字、又同在 Buenos Aires，专
门诱你混省长与市长。
借用原文：Mr. Scioli is governor of Buenos Aires province

questions.stem: What does Mr. Macri want to do?
options: C) Carry out social welfare programs.
D) Seek the help of economic reform.

explain.定位:
Mr. Macri says he wants to lift some financial controls and trade restrictions in an effort to
help the country's economy.
马克里表示他想解除部分金融管制和贸易限制，以提振国家经济。
explain.信号:
wants to 表意愿即主张落点。答案信号是表意愿的 Mr. Macri says he wants to lift some
financial controls，wants to 后跟的动作就是他的主张；动词 lift（解除/放开）是方向关
键，必须听准是放不是收。
explain.替换:
lift some financial controls ↔ Lift some financial controls.
动作短语整体对应
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
Tighten trade restrictions. 借了录音里的 trade restrictions，但原文是 lift some
financial controls and trade restrictions——Macri 要 lift（放开）贸易限制，选项却说
tighten（收紧），方向反了，是典型 "原词在、方向反"。
借用原文：lift some financial controls and trade restrictions
C) 张冠李戴
Carry out social welfare programs. 取自录音 social welfare programs，但那是描述
Scioli 所守的 kirchnerism 信条，不是 Macri 的主张，把别人的政策记到 Macri 头上。
借用原文：social welfare programs and defense of the working class
D) 张冠李戴
Seek the help of economic reform. 化用录音 he will seek a more measured approach
to economic reform，但 seek…economic reform 说的是 Scioli，不是 Macri；且原文是
"更稳健地推进改革"，并非 "寻求改革之助"。
借用原文：Mr. Scioli adds that he will seek a more measured approach to economic reform

questions.stem: What was said about the Argentine election law?
options: A) A candidate with over 45 percent of the vote could win the presidency.
B) A candidate who has 10 more points over the second wins the presidency.
C) Any candidate who wins the most of the vote could be the winner.
D) Any candidate who wins at least 40 percent of the vote gets elected.

explain.定位:
Under Argentine law, a candidate must have more than 45 percent of the vote to be declared
the winner. A candidate can also win with at least 40 percent of the vote and a margin of 10
points over the next candidate.
根据阿根廷法律，候选人得票须超过 45% 方可被宣布为获胜者；候选人也可凭至少 40% 的
得票率、且领先次名 10 个百分点而获胜。
explain.信号:
规定句式 must have 领出门槛。答案信号是讲规则的句式 a candidate must have more
than 45 percent of the vote to be declared the winner，must have…to be declared
直接给出第一条当选门槛；其后的 can also win 引出第二条。两条都要听全。
explain.替换:
must have more than 45 percent of the vote to be declared the winner ↔
A candidate with over 45 percent of the vote could win the presidency.
more than = over，含义对应
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
A candidate who has 10 more points over the second wins the presidency. 盗用录音
a margin of 10 points over the next candidate，但原文 10 个点是第二条规则的附加条
件，前提还得 at least 40 percent；选项只取 10 点、丢掉 40% 门槛，把条件拆错了。
借用原文：at least 40 percent of the vote and a margin of 10 points over the next candidate
C) 与原文相反
Any candidate who wins the most of the vote could be the winner. 说 "得票最多即当
选"，但录音规则是要过 45%（或 40%+领先10点），并非简单多数；本则新闻里 Scioli 票
最多却仍要进入第二轮，恰恰反证该规则不成立。
借用原文：must have more than 45 percent of the vote to be declared the winner
D) 原词陷阱
Any candidate who wins at least 40 percent of the vote gets elected. 盗用录音 at
least 40 percent of the vote，但原文这条 40% 必须再加 a margin of 10 points over
the next candidate 才当选；选项只留 40%、丢掉领先 10 点的并列条件，同样是拆错条
件。
借用原文：at least 40 percent of the vote and a margin of 10 points over the next candidate

questions.stem: What does the man say about Chinese?
options: A) It is more difficult to learn than English.
B) It is used by more people than English.
C) It will be as commonly used as English.
D) It will eventually become a world language.

explain.定位:
For one thing, it's so commonly used—the only language that is used by more people
is Chinese.
一来，它(英语)使用极广——唯一比它使用人数更多的语言是中文。
explain.信号:
被问者的直接应答+唯一性措辞。这是男士回应『英语为何会成世界语言』的应答句，且用
了 the only language that is used by more people 这种『唯一』措辞点名中文，应答方
+唯一性强调，正是答案句信号。
explain.替换:
the only language that is used by more people is Chinese ↔
It is used by more people than English
同义改写：唯一用得更多=用的人比英语多
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
录音确有谈『难学』，但 Many students find English a difficult language to learn. 说的
是英语难学，本项却把『难学』安到中文头上说 It is more difficult to learn than
English.，是张冠李戴。
借用原文：Many students find English a difficult language to learn.
C) 未提及
It will be as commonly used as English. 声称中文会和英语一样常用，录音只比了当下使
用人数(中文更多)，从未说两者将来会一样常用，属未提及。
D) 张冠李戴
It will eventually become a world language. 这句『将成为世界语言』在录音里是说英语
的(开篇 Why do you say English will become the world language?)，本题问的是中
文，搬过来即张冠李戴。
借用原文：Why do you say English will become the world language?

questions.stem: What made English a widely-used language?
options: A) Its loan words from many languages.
B) Its popularity with the common people.
C) The influence of the British Empire.
D) The effect of the Industrial Revolution.

explain.定位:
It's spoken in many countries of the world because of the British Empire, and now of course,
that's the influence of America as well.
因为大英帝国，英语在世界许多国家被使用；当然，现在也有美国的影响。
explain.信号:
因果信号 because of。女士问 Why do so many people speak English? 后，男士用
because of the British Empire 直接给出原因，because of 就是这道原因题的答案信号。
explain.替换:
because of the British Empire ↔ The influence of the British Empire
几乎原词：『因为大英帝国』=『大英帝国的影响』
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
Its loan words from many languages. 借的是录音后面讲词汇时的 it has a very
international vocabulary，那是英语的『优势』，不是它『广为使用』的原因，答非所
问。
借用原文：it has a very international vocabulary
B) 答非所问
Its popularity with the common people. 蹭的是末段 only the common people spoke
English，那是解释语法为何简单的背景，和『英语为何广用』无关，答非所问。
借用原文：only the common people spoke English
D) 未提及
The effect of the Industrial Revolution. 听着像合理的历史原因，但录音从头到尾没出现
Industrial Revolution，属未提及。

questions.stem: What is said to be special about English vocabulary?
options: A) It includes a lot of words from other languages.
B) It has a growing number of newly coined words.
C) It can be easily picked up by overseas travellers.
D) It is the largest among all languages in the world.

explain.定位:
Well, first of all, it has a very international vocabulary. It has many German, Dutch, French,
Spanish and Italian words in it.
首先，它有非常国际化的词汇，里面有许多德语、荷兰语、法语、西班牙语和意大利语
的词。
explain.信号:
被问者罗列佐证的应答句。男士在 first of all 后直接给词汇特点，并以 many German,
Dutch, French, Spanish and Italian words 一连串语言名作证，是承载答案的应答+举
证句。
explain.替换:
It has many German, Dutch, French, Spanish and Italian words in it. ↔
It includes a lot of words from other languages.
具体外语名概括成『其他语言』
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
It has a growing number of newly coined words. 讲的是新造词数量增长，录音只说英语
含大量外来词，从未提『新造词』，属未提及。
C) 答非所问
It can be easily picked up by overseas travellers. 蹭了录音 English speakers have
travelled a lot 里的 travel，但录音说的是说英语者四处旅行带回词汇，不是『海外旅行者
容易学会英语』，答非所问。
借用原文：English speakers have travelled a lot
D) 张冠李戴
It is the largest among all languages in the world. 用 the largest 制造『英语词汇量最
大』的印象，但录音里被说『使用人数最多』的是中文(见 the only language that is used
by more people is Chinese)，且从没说英语词汇量最大，张冠李戴又夸大。
借用原文：the only language that is used by more people is Chinese

questions.stem: What does the man say is the second advantage of English?
options: A) It has many international words.
B) It can be pronounced easily.
C) Its grammar is very simple.
D) It has no different dialects.

explain.定位:
It's that English grammar is really quite easy. For example, it doesn't have dozens of different
endings for its nouns, adjectives and verbs.
那就是英语语法相当简单。比如，它的名词、形容词、动词不像别的语言那样有几十种不同
的词尾变化。
explain.信号:
回应『另一个优势』的应答句。女士追问 what's the other advantage of English?，男士
紧接着答 English grammar is really quite easy，这是对『第二个优势』提问的直接应
答，即答案句。
explain.替换:
English grammar is really quite easy ↔ Its grammar is very simple.
easy=simple 的同义替换
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
It has many international words. 对应的是录音第一个优势 it has a very international
vocabulary，本题问第二个优势，拿第一点来答即错位。
借用原文：it has a very international vocabulary
B) 未提及
It can be pronounced easily. 谈发音容易，录音讲的两个优势是词汇国际化和语法简单，
从未提发音，属未提及。
D) 过度推断
It has no different dialects. 没有直接原文支撑——录音说的是语法没有几十种 different
endings(词尾变化)，并非『没有不同方言』，把『词尾』偷换成『方言』属过度推断。
借用原文：dozens of different endings for its nouns, adjectives and verbs

questions.stem: What is the woman's purpose in making the phone call?
options: B) To apply for a job.

explain.定位:
My name is Jane Kingsbury of GPF Ltd. Um, we need some supplies for our designer office.
我叫简·金斯伯里，来自 GPF 有限公司。嗯，我们的设计室需要采购一些用品。
explain.信号:
自报家门后的来意句。女方先自报身份，紧接着 we need some supplies for our
designer office 就是亮明来意的那句——目的题的答案信号正是这种通话开头"我是谁＋我
要什么"的结构。后文她逐项询价、确认价格，进一步坐实是来订货而非别的。
explain.替换:
we need some supplies for our designer office ↔ To place an order.
需要采购用品＝下订单
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
To return some goods.（退货）与原文相反——女方是来"需要"东西、要买进，不是退
回；全程没有任何已购货物要退的内容。
B) 未提及
To apply for a job.（求职）原文毫无线索，女方一上来就谈买东西，与应聘无关。
D) 过度推断
To make a complaint.（投诉）容易因女方一连串追问（价格、含税否、材质、送货）听起
来"挑剔"而误选，但她全程在询价、议货，是订货前的正常打听，并无任何不满表达。
借用原文：how long does it take to deliver?

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
options: A) He has become somewhat impatient with the woman.
B) He is not familiar with the exact details of the goods.
C) He has not worked in the sales department for long.
D) He works on a part-time basis for the company.

explain.定位:
Oh, I'm not sure. Most of the prices do. Yes, I think it does. / Oh, I don't know. I think it's a
sort of plastic stuff these days.
哦，我不太确定。大部分价格是含的。嗯，我想是含的。／哦，我不知道。我想这年头大概
是种塑料材质吧。
explain.信号:
反复出现的"我不确定/我不知道"。男方被问到是否含税时 I'm not sure、被问材质时 I
don't know，对货品细节一问三不知。这种"同一信号在答问中反复出现"就是答案信号
——细节归纳题要靠多处一致的表现而非单句来判。
explain.替换:
I'm not sure ↔ He is not familiar with the exact details of the goods.
屡答不知＝不熟货品细节
I don't know. I think it's a sort of plastic stuff ↔ not familiar with the exact details of the goods
连材质都靠猜
explain.排除:
A) 过度推断
He has become somewhat impatient with the woman.（对女方不耐烦）易因他屡屡"不
知道"而被听成"嫌烦"，但他始终在配合作答、还反问 So do you want the drawing board
then?，并无不耐烦的措辞或语气，属脑补。
C) 未提及
He has not worked in the sales department for long.（在销售部没干多久）听着像
是"不熟业务"的合理解释，但原文只说他不管接文具订单 I only do the equipment，从没
提他入职时间长短，是无中生有的推因。
D) 偷换概念
He works on a part-time basis for the company.（兼职）易被他"只管设备、不接文具
单"勾出"他大概只干一部分活"的联想，但 I only do the equipment 说的是分工不同，不
等于兼职，原文从未提工作是否为 part-time。
借用原文：I only do the equipment

questions.stem: What does the man say about delivery?
options: A) It is not his responsibility.
B) It will be free for large orders.
C) It costs £15 more for express delivery.
D) It depends on a number of factors.

explain.定位:
Oh, I couldn't really say. It depends on how much work we've got and how many other orders
there are to send out, you know.
哦，这我真说不准。要看我们手头有多少活、还有多少别的订单要发出去，你懂的。
explain.信号:
被问送货后的直接应答。女方问 how long does it take to deliver?，男方紧接着的应答
It depends on how much work we've got and how many other orders 就是答案句
——对话题的答案信号正是"被问者对该问题的直接回答"，问送货，答案就落在他答送货的
这句。
explain.替换:
It depends on how much work we've got and how many other orders there are ↔
It depends on a number of factors.
罗列的多种情况＝若干因素
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
It is not his responsibility.（这不归他管）盗用了后文 I only do the equipment——
但"不归他管"说的是文具订单不归他接，并非送货；把另一处的"不归他管"安到"送货"头
上，属张冠李戴。
借用原文：I only do the equipment
B) 未提及
It will be free for large orders.（大单免送货费）原文从未提送货是否收费、更没说大单免
费，是凭"商家常有大单优惠"的常识编出来的。
C) 原词陷阱
It costs £15 more for express delivery. 死盗原文 the 45 costs 15 pounds more 里
的"15 pounds more"——但那"贵 15 镑"说的是 DO45 比 DO44 贵，是型号差价，跟送
货、跟 express 毫无关系。听到"15"就选，正中原词陷阱。
借用原文：the 45 costs 15 pounds more

questions.stem: What does the woman say she will possibly do tomorrow?
options: A) Report the information to her superior.
B) Pay a visit to the saleswoman in charge.
C) Ring back when she comes to a decision.
D) Make inquiries with some other companies.

explain.定位:
OK, well, perhaps I ring back tomorrow. / Oh, I have to think about it. Thanks very much. I'll
let you know.
好吧，那我也许明天再打回来。／哦，我得再考虑考虑。非常感谢，我会再通知你的。
explain.信号:
结尾告别前的安排句。女方在挂电话前说 perhaps I ring back tomorrow，又说 I have to
think about it…I'll let you know——"想好了再回电"。结尾告别处带 perhaps/I'll 的安排
句，正是这类"接下来做什么"题的答案信号。
explain.替换:
perhaps I ring back tomorrow ↔ Ring back when she comes to a decision.
明天回电＝想好后回电
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Report the information to her superior.（向上级汇报）原文没有任何"上司/汇报"的内
容，她只说自己再考虑，是无中生有。
B) 原词陷阱
Pay a visit to the saleswoman in charge.（去拜访负责的销售女士）易被男方提到的 The
girl that takes orders for supplies 勾出联想，但原文只说那位负责接单的姑娘今早不在，
女方从没说要去拜访她；"visit"原文也没有。
借用原文：The girl that takes orders for supplies isn't here this morning
D) 未提及
Make inquiries with some other companies.（向别家公司打听）听着像"货比三家"的合
理之举，但女方只说自己再想想、想好回电，根本没提去问别的公司，是常识脑补。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about kites?
options: A) No one knows exactly where they were first made.
B) No one knows for sure when they came into being.
C) No one knows for what purpose they were invented.
D) No one knows what they will look like in the future.

explain.定位:
No one knows for sure just how old kites are.
没有人确切知道风筝到底有多古老。
explain.信号:
开篇"No one knows for sure"的不确定语气。篇章第一句就是 No one knows for sure
just how old kites are.，"No one knows for sure"（没人确切知道）是醒目的不确定信
号；篇章独白常把核心信息放在开篇，这句既点题又承认"年代说不清"，正是答案句。
explain.替换:
just how old kites are ↔ when they came into being
"多古老"="何时产生"，同义改写
No one knows for sure ↔ No one knows for sure
前半句原词照搬，差异只在维度词
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音后面确有 These first kites were probably made of wood. 提到"最初的风筝"，A 借
first made 这个词造出"没人知道在哪儿first made"；但原文 made 谈的是材质
（wood），且"说不清"的是年代不是产地，A 答非所问。
借用原文：These first kites were probably made of wood.
C) 原词陷阱
原文有 Early kites were built for certain uses.，C 借"用途/发明目的"做文章说"没人知道
为何发明"；可原文非但没说目的不明，反而清楚列了运绳过河等用途，C 与原文相反。
借用原文：Early kites were built for certain uses.
D) 未提及
D 说"没人知道未来风筝长什么样"，但整段只讲历史与古今用途，结尾是 kite flying is sure
to remain an entertaining and popular sport，谈的是会继续流行，完全没谈未来外形，
D 属未提及。

questions.stem: What did ancient Chinese use kites to do?
options: B) Measure the speed of wind.

explain.定位:
In ancient China, they were used to carry ropes to cross rivers.
在古代中国，风筝被用来运送绳索以横渡河流。
explain.信号:
限定词 In ancient China + 用途结构 were used to。In ancient China, they were used
to carry ropes to cross rivers. 一句里，"In ancient China"正好对上题干的 ancient
Chinese，"were used to"是表用途的信号结构，两者叠加把这句标成答案句。
explain.替换:
carry ropes to cross rivers ↔ Carry ropes across rivers
to cross rivers = across rivers，近义改写
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
原文谈到风筝用 silk，也讲它"flew over the enemy's camp"，但从未提"测风速"。B 利
用"风筝—风"的常识联想造测风速，属未提及。
C) 偷换概念
原文确有将军 flew musical kites over the enemy's camp 让敌人误以为是天使警告而逃，
C 借这个"用声音影响敌人"的情节改成"传递秘密信息"；但那是用声音吓退敌军，并非传送
密信，C 偷换概念。
借用原文：Legend tells of one General who flew musical kites over the enemy's camp.
D) 原词陷阱
原文 believing the sounds to be the warning voices of angels 出现 warning，D 顺势
造"用风筝报危险"；但 warning 是敌人对声音的误解，是"让敌人以为有警告而逃跑"，并非
中国人拿风筝去报危险，D 张冠李戴。
借用原文：the enemy fled, believing the sounds to be the warning voices of angels

questions.stem: Why did Benjamin Franklin fly a kite in the storm?
options: A) To protect houses against lightning.
B) To test the effects of the lightning rod.
C) To find out the strength of silk for kites.
D) To prove that lightning is electricity.

explain.定位:
Benjamin Franklin used a kite to prove that lightning is electricity. He flew the kite in the
storm. He did this in order to draw lightning from the clouds.
本杰明·富兰克林用风筝来证明闪电是电。他在暴风雨中放风筝，这样做是为了从云中引出
闪电。
explain.信号:
目的信号 to prove / in order to。used a kite to prove that lightning is electricity 里
的 "to prove" 与 He did this in order to draw lightning from the clouds 里的 "in order
to" 都是直白的目的信号，连续两句都在讲"为什么放"，正是答案句。
explain.替换:
to prove that lightning is electricity ↔ To prove that lightning is electricity
原文目的句几乎原词对应选项
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
原文结尾 it led to the invention of the lightning rod，避雷针确能护房防雷，A 借此
说"放风筝是为护房防雷"；但护房是后来避雷针的作用，不是当初放风筝的目的，A 把"后续
结果"当"当初目的"。
借用原文：it led to the invention of the lightning rod
B) 原词陷阱
B 说放风筝是为"测试避雷针的效果"，可避雷针是这件事之后才被发明的（later on, it led
to the invention of the lightning rod），放风筝时避雷针还不存在，谈不上测试，B 与时
间线相悖。
借用原文：But later on, it led to the invention of the lightning rod.
C) 原词陷阱
原文 He tied a metal key and a strip of silk to the kite line 提到 silk，C 顺手造"为测风
筝丝线的强度"；但 silk 在这里是实验材料，作用是 The silk ribbon would stop the
lightning from passing through his body（绝缘护身），跟"测丝线强度"毫无关系，C 答
非所问。
借用原文：The silk ribbon would stop the lightning from passing through his body.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about herself?
options: B) She can speak several languages.
C) She was trained to be an interpreter.
D) She was born with a talent for languages.

explain.定位:
I have learned many languages, but I've not mastered them the way the professional
interpreter or translator has.
我学过很多种语言，但我并没有像专业口译员或笔译员那样把它们掌握到精通。
explain.信号:
开篇自述句 + 转折 but 划清边界。这是篇章开头说话人的自我介绍句，本身就是答案高发
位；更关键的是 but I've not mastered them the way the professional interpreter or
translator has 用 but 把"会多门"与"没到专业口译水平"划开，正好用来肯定 B、否定 C。
explain.替换:
I have learned many languages ↔ She can speak several languages.
many languages ≈ several languages 且人称换说
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
A 说她 enjoys teaching languages（喜欢教语言），但原文是 I have learned many
languages——是"学"不是"教"，把 learn 偷换成 teach，听到 languages 就选会上当。
借用原文：I have learned many languages
C) 与原文相反
C 说她 was trained to be an interpreter（受训当口译员），但原文紧接着 but 否定：I've
not mastered them the way the professional interpreter or translator has——她恰恰
强调自己"不像专业口译那样精通"，选项与原文相反，且盗用了 interpreter 这个原词来诱
选。
借用原文：I've not mastered them the way the professional interpreter or translator has
D) 未提及
D 说她 was born with a talent for languages（天生有语言天赋），但原文只讲她"学
过"很多语言，从没说这是天生的，属凭"会多门语言"脑补出"天赋"，原文无据。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about many people who have lived overseas for a while?
options: A) They acquire an immunity to culture shock.
B) They would like to live abroad permanently.
C) They want to learn as many foreign languages as possible.
D) They have an intense interest in cross-cultural interactions.

explain.定位:
Like many people who have lived overseas for a while, I simply got crazy about it. I can't
imagine living my professional or social life without international interactions.
像许多在国外住过一阵子的人一样，我简直对它着了迷。我无法想象自己的职业生活或社交
生活里没有跨国互动。
explain.信号:
题干同款词 like…overseas for a while 顺听定位 + 后句解释。录音里 Like many
people who have lived overseas for a while 与题干用词几乎一字不差，是最强定位信
号；紧接的 I can't imagine living my professional or social life without international
interactions 用"无法想象没有跨国互动"道出这群人的共同特点。
explain.替换:
I can't imagine living my professional or social life without international interactions ↔
They have an intense interest in cross-cultural interactions.
"无法想象没有"=强烈喜爱；international≈cross-cultural
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
A 说他们 acquire an immunity to culture shock（获得对文化冲击的免疫力），原文通篇
没提 culture shock，是凭"长期在外"脑补出的引申，无原文支持。
B) 偷换概念
B 说他们 would like to live abroad permanently（想永久住在国外），原文虽说爱往外
跑，却只到 If I had the time and money, I would live for a year in as many countries
as possible——是"每国住一年"而非"永久定居"，permanently 把程度抬过头了。
借用原文：If I had the time and money, I would live for a year in as many countries as possible
C) 原词陷阱
C 说他们 want to learn as many foreign languages as possible（想学尽可能多的外
语），原文确有 as many…as possible 的句式，但配的是 live for a year in as many
countries as possible——是"住尽量多的国家"，不是"学尽量多的语言"，盗用句式张冠李
戴。
借用原文：live for a year in as many countries as possible

questions.stem: How did the speaker's experience of living in Vienna benefit her?
options: A) She became an expert in horse racing.
B) She got a chance to visit several European countries.
C) She was able to translate for a German sports judge.
D) She learned to appreciate classical music.

explain.定位:
Once, just after I returned from my year in Vienna, I was asked to translate for a German
judge at an Olympic level horse event and learned a lot about the sport.
有一次，就在我结束在维也纳一年的生活回来后不久，我被请去为一场奥运级别的马术赛事
中的一位德国裁判做翻译，还学到了很多关于这项运动的知识。
explain.信号:
时间锚 after…Vienna + 结果信号 I was asked to。just after I returned from my year
in Vienna 是与题干"living in Vienna"对应的时间锚，听到就知道答案临近；紧跟的 I was
asked to translate for a German judge 是"她因此得到什么"的结果句，正是受益所在。
explain.替换:
I was asked to translate for a German judge at an Olympic level horse event ↔
She was able to translate for a German sports judge.
Olympic level horse event judge = sports judge；asked to=was able to
explain.排除:
A) 过度推断
A 说她 became an expert in horse racing（成了赛马专家），原文只说 learned a lot
about the sport（学到不少关于这项运动的知识），"学到不少"远不到"专家"，且 horse
event 被偷换成 horse racing，程度被抬高。
借用原文：learned a lot about the sport
B) 未提及
B 说她 got a chance to visit several European countries（得到游览几个欧洲国家的机
会），原文只提到 Vienna（维也纳，奥地利）一地，从没说她借此游历多个欧洲国家，
是"住维也纳"引出的合理脑补。
D) 未提及
D 说她 learned to appreciate classical music（学会欣赏古典音乐），"维也纳=音乐之
都"是常识联想，但原文讲的受益是做翻译，根本没提音乐，纯属背景知识脑补。

questions.stem: What was the speaker asked to do in the Japanese studio?
options: A) Taste the beef and give her comment.
B) Take part in a cooking competition.
C) Teach vocabulary for food in English.
D) Give cooking lessons on Western food.

explain.定位:
In Japan, once when I was in the studio audience of a TV cooking show, I was asked to go up
on the stage and taste the beef dish that was being prepared and tell what I thought.
在日本，有一次我坐在一档电视烹饪节目的观众席里，被请上台去品尝正在烹制的牛肉菜
肴，并说说我的感受。
explain.信号:
场景锚 Japanese studio + 结果信号 I was asked to。when I was in the studio
audience of a TV cooking show 对应题干的 Japanese studio，是定位锚；紧跟的 I was
asked to go up on the stage and taste the beef dish…and tell what I thought 由 I
was asked to 引出真正被要求做的两个动作：尝牛肉、说感受。
explain.替换:
taste the beef dish that was being prepared and tell what I thought ↔
Taste the beef and give her comment.
taste the beef 原词保留；tell what I thought=give her comment
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
B 说她 Take part in a cooking competition（参加烹饪比赛），原文是 cooking show
（烹饪节目）不是 competition，她只是观众被请上台尝一口，没有比赛，把 cooking 这
个原词盗来夸成"比赛"。
借用原文：a TV cooking show
C) 答非所问
C 说她 Teach vocabulary for food in English（用英语教食物词汇），原文她是用日语
speaking in Japanese about how delicious the beef was 评价牛肉，既不是"教词汇"也
不是"用英语"，方向全错。
借用原文：speaking in Japanese about how delicious the beef was
D) 过度推断
D 说她 Give cooking lessons on Western food（教西餐烹饪课），原文她只是被请上台
尝牛肉、说感受，并未授课讲西餐，cooking 原词被借去夸大成"上课"。
借用原文：taste the beef dish that was being prepared and tell what I thought

questions.stem: What do we learn about Ben Carsen?
options: A) He had only a third-grade education.
B) He once threatened to kill his teacher.
C) He grew up in a poor single-parent family.
D) He often helped his mother do housework.

explain.定位:
Dr. Ben Carsen grew up in a poor single-parent household in Detroit.
本·卡森博士在底特律一个贫困的单亲家庭里长大。
explain.信号:
篇章开篇第一句即交代出身。人物故事的第一句往往直接交代背景，这里 grew up in a
poor single-parent household 就是身世落点，听到"grew up in…"这种背景交代句要立
刻锁定。

questions.stem: It will not be difficult to make learning a source of joy if educators change their way of thinking.
questions.passage:
Joy: A Subject Schools Lack

Becoming educated should not require giving up pleasure

A) When Jonathan Swift proposed, in 1729, that the people of Ireland eat their children, he insisted it would solve three problems at once: feed the hungry masses, reduce the population during a severe depression, and stimulate the restaurant business. Even as a satire(讽刺), it seems disgusting and shocking in America with its child-centered culture. But actually, the country is closer to his proposal than you might think.

B) If you spend much time with educators and policy makers, you'll hear a lot of the following words: "standards," "results," "skills," "self-control," "accountability," and so on. I have visited some of the newer supposedly "effective" schools, where children shout slogans in order to learn self-control or must stand behind their desk when they can't sit still.

C) A look at what goes on in most classrooms these days makes it abundantly clear that when people think about education, they are not thinking about what it feels like to be a child, or what makes childhood an important and valuable stage of life in its own right.

D) I'm a mother of three, a teacher, and a developmental psychologist. So I've watched a lot of children—talking, playing, arguing, eating, studying, and being young. Here's what I've come to understand. The thing that sets children apart from adults is not their ignorance, nor their lack of skills. It's their enormous capacity for joy. Think of a 3-year-old lost in the pleasures of finding out what he can and cannot sink in the bathtub, a 5-year-old beside herself with the thrill of putting together strings of nonsensical words with her best friends, or an 11-year-old completely absorbed in a fascinating comic strip. A child's ability to become deeply absorbed in something, and derive intense pleasure from that absorption, is something adults spend the rest of their lives trying to return to.

E) A friend told me the following story. One day, when he went to get his 7-year-old son from soccer practice, his kid greeted him with a downcast face and a sad voice. The coach had criticized him for not focusing on his soccer drills. The little boy walked out of the school with his head and shoulders hanging down. He seemed wrapped in sadness. But just before he reached the car door, he suddenly stopped, crouching(蹲伏) down to peer at something on the sidewalk. His face went down lower and lower, and then, with complete joy he called out, "Dad. Come here. This is the strangest bug I've ever seen. It has, like, a million legs. Look at this. It's amazing." He looked up at his father, his features overflowing with energy and delight. "Can't we stay here for just a minute? I want to find out what he does with all those legs. This is the coolest ever."

F) The traditional view of such moments is that they constitute a charming but irrelevant byproduct of youth—something to be pushed aside to make room for more important qualities, like perseverance(坚持不懈), obligation, and practicality. Yet moments like this one are just the kind of intense absorption and pleasure adults spend the rest of their lives seeking. Human lives are governed by the desire to experience joy. Becoming educated should not require giving up joy but rather lead to finding joy in new kinds of things: reading novels instead of playing with small figures, conducting experiments instead of sinking cups in the bathtub, and debating serious issues rather than stringing together nonsense words, for example. In some cases, schools should help children find new, more grown-up ways of doing the same things that are constant sources of joy: making art, making friends, making decisions.

G) Building on a child's ability to feel joy, rather than pushing it aside, wouldn't be that hard. It would just require a shift in the education world's mindset(思维模式). Instead of trying to get children to work hard, why not focus on getting them to take pleasure in meaningful, productive activity, like making things, working with others, exploring ideas, and solving problems? These focuses are not so different from the things in which they delight.

H) Before you brush this argument aside as rubbish, or think of joy as an unaffordable luxury in a nation where there is awful poverty, low academic achievement, and high dropout rates, think again. The more horrible the school circumstances, the more important pleasure is to achieving any educational success.

I) Many of the assignments and rules teachers come up with, often because they are pressured by their administrators, treat pleasure and joy as the enemies of competence and responsibility. The assumption is that children shouldn't chat in the classroom because it hinders hard work; instead, they should learn to delay gratification(快乐) so that they can pursue abstract goals, like going to college.

J) Not only is this a boring and awful way to treat children, it makes no sense educationally. Decades of research have shown that in order to acquire skills and real knowledge in school, kids need to want to learn. You can force a child to stay in his or her seat, fill out a worksheet, or practice division. But you can't force the child to think carefully, enjoy books, digest complex information, or develop a taste for learning. To make that happen, you have to help the child find pleasure in learning—to see school as a source of joy.

K) Adults tend to talk about learning as if it were medicine: unpleasant, but necessary and good for you. Why not instead think of learning as if it were food—something so valuable to humans that they have evolved to experience it as a pleasure?

L) Joy should not be trained out of children or left for after-school programs. The more difficult a child's life circumstances, the more important it is for that child to find joy in his or her classroom. "Pleasure" is not a dirty word. And it doesn't run counter to the goals of public education. It is, in fact, the precondition.

questions.stem: What does the author think of time displayed everywhere?
options: B) It is a convenience for work and life.
C) It may have a negative effect on creative work.
D) It clearly indicates the fast pace of modern life.
questions.passage:
When it's five o'clock, people leave their office. The length of the workday, for many workers, is defined by time. They leave when the clock tells them they're done.

These days, the time is everywhere: not just on clocks or watches, but on cell-phones and computers. That may be a bad thing, particularly at work. New research shows that clock-based work schedules hinder morale(士气) and creativity.

Clock-timers organize their day by blocks of minutes and hours. For example: a meeting from 9 a.m. to 10 a.m., research from 10 a.m. to noon, etc. On the other hand, task-timers have a list of things they want to accomplish. They work down the list, each task starts when the previous task is completed. It is said that all of us employ a mix of both these types of planning.

What, then, are the effects of thinking about time in these different ways? Does one make us more productive? Better at the tasks at hand? Happier? In experiments conducted by Tamar Avnet and Anne-Laure Sellier, they had participants organize different activities—from project planning, holiday shopping, to yoga—by time or to-do list to measure how they performed under "clock time" vs "task time." They found clock timers to be more efficient but less happy because they felt little control over their lives. Task timers are happier and more creative, but less productive. They tend to enjoy the moment when something good is happening, and seize opportunities that come up.

The researchers argue that task-based organizing tends to be undervalued and under-supported in business culture. Smart companies, they believe, will try to bake more task-based planning into their strategies.

This might be a small change to the way we view work and the office, but the researchers argue that it challenges a widespread characteristic of the economy: work organized by clock time. While most people will still probably need, and be, to some extent, clock-timers, task-based timing should be used when performing a job that requires more creativity. It'll make those tasks easier, and the task doers will be happier.

questions.stem: What does the well-known columnist's remark about Martha Stewart suggest?

Many of these penalties are imposed regardless of the seriousness of the offense or the person's individual circumstances. Laws can restrict or ban voting, access to public housing, and professional and business licensing. They can affect a person's ability to get a job and qualification for benefits.

In all, more than 45,000 laws and rules serve to exclude vast numbers of people from fully participating in American life.

The saying goes that listening is more important than talking. From my perspective, this remark makes good
sense, because only by paying close attention to others' opinions can we truly understand a situation and
respond wisely.
A good case in point is teamwork. In a group project I once joined, our leader kept talking and ignored our
suggestions, and the plan soon fell apart. Later, another leader chose to listen carefully to every member's idea
before making a decision, and the task was completed smoothly. History offers a similar lesson: many wise
leaders, such as ancient emperors who welcomed honest advice, achieved great success precisely because they
were attentive listeners rather than endless talkers.

understanding. Therefore, we should learn to close our mouths and open our ears before we rush to speak.
